items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The reason Gil Birnes name is on there is he condensed those down to maybe a hundred pages each book

ctx.x: So let’s talk about what motivated you to get into writing books and exercises and things, and did you do that for yourself initially?

When I was working for my dad in the music store, I noticed that there wasn’t too much material in those days for drums. It was always, here’s how you hold the left hand, the right hand. They didn’t even talk about matched grip then. It was all conventional grip. So I decided to write some exercises that would help drummers – not only drummers, but brass instrument players and reed players, because rhythm is part of their lives too. So I wrote 400 pages on 4/4 only, 400 pages on 3/4 only, 400 pages on 2/4. Then I…
A little less than a hundred: 91 in this one. That’s Modern Reading Texts. And then the Odd Time Reading Texts, there are – it seems like a few more. Yeah. There’s about 129, 130 pages here.
